_purpose: AI-entry-point inventory (Wave 3b security posture). Every Tauri command in commands.rs that reaches the model provider (ai::generate / ai::generate_stream / ai::governed_turn) MUST be listed here with an honest classification. A command 'reaches' a provider either by calling it DIRECTLY or by calling a NON-command pub helper (defined in the same file) that calls it, resolved ONE call-hop deep — so a new ungoverned surface cannot hide the provider call behind a helper. tools/check_ai_surfaces.py fails CI closed on any unclassified provider-reaching command, stale entry, a policy entry that is not a #[tauri::command], an untracked non-governed surface, or a 'governed' surface that actually reaches a generic provider entry (directly or via a helper). This is inventory + drift-prevention only; it does NOT change the security architecture and does NOT assert any surface is governed that is not.

governance_states.governed: routes ONLY through ai::governed_turn (full governed chain: challenge -> prepare -> execute -> verify -> persist); MUST NOT reach the generic ai::generate / ai::generate_stream, whether directly or one call-hop through a pub helper.
governance_states.ungoverned_tracked: reaches a generic provider entry today (directly or via a one-hop pub helper); carries a 'tracking' reference to the task/wave that will govern or gate it. Honest current state while Wave 3b (isolated trusted signer) is pending.
governance_states.excluded: deliberately outside the production governed set (e.g. dev-only), with 'tracking'.

_resolution: Provider reachability is resolved one call-hop deep: command -> (optional) non-command pub helper in commands.rs -> ai::generate / ai::generate_stream / ai::governed_turn. Helpers themselves are NOT policy entries (only #[tauri::command] fns are surfaces); they are resolution inputs. Deeper chains (helper -> helper -> provider) are out of scope of this gate by design.
